subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — shared vs dedicated (noisy neighbor & SLOs)
messages:

Subject: Post-call recap — deployment mode & isolation questions

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

- Primary goals you mentioned: predictable 99th pct latency for low-latency features, data isolation for customer PII, and minimizing cost.
- Key concern: noisy neighbor behavior during your nightly batch jobs causing latency spikes for online requests.

Questions for scoping:
1) What’s your expected online qps / tokens per second during peak? (ballpark is fine)
2) Are there regulatory constraints that push you to a private VPC/on-prem deployment vs a dedicated pool?
3) Any required audit artifacts (SOC 2 evidence, audit log retention length)?

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep dive with Marissa to map traffic profile and SLOs (30–45m).
- We’ll attach our Dedicated SLA draft and a deployment diagram.
- If Dedicated looks like the right fit, Rishi can put together a pilot & pricing estimate.

I’ve copied Marissa and Rishi to handle the technical and commercial questions.

Thanks —
Priyom
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment mode & isolation questions

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the recap. Quick answers:
- Peak online traffic: ~120 qps, roughly 1.2M tokens/day; spike pattern is mostly business hours 9am–6pm PST but we see 2x spikes during campaign windows.
- Nightly batch jobs: heavy embeddings/rehit processing that coincides with midnight–2am UTC; these have caused 95th/99th latency regressions for front-door requests in our canary tests.
- Compliance: need SOC2 evidence and audit log retention for 12 months; also want to understand network isolation options.

Primary question: can you guarantee isolation such that noisy neighbor batch jobs will not bump our 99th percentile latency for online inference? If not, what are the mitigation options and expected SLOs?

Happy to take the tech deep dive — can do next Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Best,
Alice
Director, AI Platforms | FinTechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment mode & isolation questions

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the details — replying with technical options and what we can commit to. High-level:

1) Hosted API (shared):
- Pros: fastest to go live, no infra management.
- Cons: noisy neighbor risk exists because requests are multiplexed across shared pools; we mitigate with request routing and dynamic autoscale but cannot provide hard isolation guarantees for 99th pct under pathological neighbor loads.

2) Dedicated capacity (recommended for your case):
- We provide reserved GPU pools that are logically and physically isolated for your account (no tenant mixing on the same instance class).
- Network isolation, dedicated KV cache warmers, and configurable autoscaling policies.
- Can offer SLA-backed SLOs for availability and latency tiers; see attached redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf (summary).
- For your profile (~120 qps; model gen-llm-0.8), with a modest reserved pool we expect 99th pct generation latency in the ~150–300ms range depending on prompt length; we can run a short bench to finalize.

3) Private VPC / on-prem:
- Best for regulated data / strict network controls. Requires more setup and a slightly longer lead time for deployment. We can ship a private control plane with customer-managed networking and integrate with your KMS.

Mitigations & recommendations:
- Dedicated capacity will eliminate noisy neighbor impact for online requests.
- If you want the lowest possible multi-tenant risk and full audit log control, Private VPC is the path.
- For your compliance ask, we can provide SOC2 artifacts and set log retention via the Private control plane / Dedicated add-on.

Questions for scoping before the deep dive:
- Typical prompt lengths / token-per-request distribution?
- Do you require on-prem (air-gapped) or is VPC acceptable?

I’ve attached the Dedicated SLA draft. Happy to walk through during the tech call and run a quick benchmark against a representative prompt set.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf (redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — pricing & pilot

Hi Alice —

Quick commercial note to set expectations ahead of the tech deep dive:
- Dedicated capacity pricing includes a monthly reserved commitment plus variable token/throughput charges for burst periods. Typical uplift vs. Hosted is ~2–3x depending on reservation level and instance type.
- Setup lead time for Dedicated (provisioning + security review) is typically 2–3 weeks; Private VPC/on-prem is 4–8 weeks depending on networking and KMS integration.
- We can run a 2–4 week pilot with a smaller reserved pool to validate 99th pct behavior and share metrics.

If you confirm target 99th pct SLO and an initial reserved GPU target (we can size on the tech call), I’ll draft a pilot statement of work and pricing. I’ll also link a short mutual action plan in HubSpot and add milestone dates.

Thanks —
Rishi
